themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis This Week
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 59 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 21.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 178% increase (z-score: 5.06)—suggesting a sudden infrastructure deterioration event across Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 59 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 21.2 weekly average (178% spike, z-score: 5.06)
Spike is statistically significant and recent—not a sustained 4-week trend but an acute this-week event
Aligns with winter weather patterns (snow/ice complaints also elevated at 918 over 90 days) but magnitude suggests localized problem beyond seasonal
reporting_angles: What specific streets are most affected? Interview residents on affected blocks and DOT to determine if potholes, flooding, or other hazards are causing complaints
Is this related to ongoing construction activity? 1,081 DOB permits filed in 90 days—have utility or construction projects damaged streets?

themes_detail.label: Building/Use Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 1.4 per week (409% increase, z-score: 5.06), indicating a possible pattern of code violations or unpermitted work emerging in the district.
evidence: 7 building/use complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly baseline (409% spike, z-score: 5.06)
High volume of DOB permits filed (1,081 in 90 days, 788 alterations) creates environment where unpermitted work could occur
Active development pipeline (395 Flatbush Avenue redevelopment in public review, Columbia Heights rezoning filed) may be creating adjacent construction violations or code conflicts
reporting_angles: What specific building/use violations are residents reporting? Are they related to illegal subdivisions, unpermitted commercial activity, or occupancy issues?
How does this spike correlate with active development projects? Interview Department of Buildings about enforcement response to the spike

themes_detail.label: Animal & Sanitation Concerns Converge
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints rose 167% (3 last week vs. 1.1 baseline, z-score: 5.67) and animal-in-park complaints jumped 273% (7 THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 baseline, z-score: 4.04), while litter basket requests spiked 550% (13 three weeks ago vs. 2.0 baseline, z-score: 6.35)—suggesting emerging sanitation and wildlife management challenges.
evidence: Dead animal complaints: 3 last week vs. 1.1 weekly average (167% increase, z-score: 5.67)
Animal-in-park complaints: 7 THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average (273% increase, z-score: 4.04)
Litter basket requests: 13 three weeks ago vs. 2.0 weekly average (550% increase, z-score: 6.35)—suggests residents perceive trash infrastructure as inadequate
reporting_angles: Are residents reporting the same parks or streets repeatedly? Map the complaints to identify hotspots and interview Parks Dept about pest control and maintenance response
Is inadequate sanitation infrastructure (litter baskets) driving animal attraction to the district? Connect with Parks and Sanitation to assess resource allocation

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting & Street Signage Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints surged 700% (4 last week vs. 0.5 baseline, z-score: 4.95) and dangling street signs jumped 344% (5 last week vs. 1.1 baseline, z-score: 4.96), suggesting both a new problem of unauthorized advertising and possible deferred maintenance of street infrastructure.
evidence: Illegal posting: 4 complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 4.95)
Dangling street signs: 5 complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (344% spike, z-score: 4.96)
Two distinct infrastructure issues converging suggests possible neglect of street maintenance or enforcement
reporting_angles: Where is illegal posting concentrated? Is this organized flyposting (event promotions, political campaigns) or general tag/graffiti? Contact NYPD and Department of Sanitation
How many dangling signs are there district-wide and how long have they been deteriorating? Request DOT inventory and maintenance records

themes_detail.label: General Construction & Plumbing Issues
themes_detail.summary: General construction/plumbing complaints rose 147% (29 last week vs. 11.8 baseline, z-score: 5.47), indicating a spike in either unpermitted construction work or failures in regulated construction activity last week.
evidence: 29 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 11.8 weekly baseline (147% increase, z-score: 5.47)
High DOB permit activity (1,081 filings in 90 days) creates environment for construction-related complaints
Overlaps with building/use violation spike this week, suggesting broader construction enforcement issue
reporting_angles: Are these complaints about noise, safety violations, or code violations during construction? Interview residents and Department of Buildings about complaint nature and enforcement timeline
Do complaints cluster around specific active development sites (395 Flatbush, 130 St. Felix, Columbia Heights rezoning areas)?
